title: Compression & Filters
text: navigate HDF5 compression effectively, helpful understand specific terminology used throughout guide broader HDF5 ecosystem: Filter: function HDF5 data pipeline transforms data written disk read disk. Pre-filter: specific type filter (like Bitshuffle) designed rearrange bytes make data mathematically compressible handing main compressor. Compressor / Codec: algorithm (e.g., Zstd, LZ4, ZFP) actually shrinks physical data footprint. Plugin: external, dynamically loaded library (e.g., ..dll file) provides HDF5 library code needed execute filter isn’t built core library. Mode: specific operational setting compressor (e.g., ZFP’s “Fixed Accuracy” mode LZ4’s “High Compression” mode).

title: Compression & Filters
text: configuring filter, must understand fundamental rules HDF5 compression: Chunking Mandatory: Compression HDF5 requires data stored “chunks.” must define chunk size dataset using H5Pset_chunk(). Applying filter contiguous dataset fail. Filter Registration (Plugins ): using bundled plugins (Zstd, LZ4, Blosc, etc.), must registered globally R session. exactly package’s .onLoad hook using hdf5lib_register_all_filters() tear .onUnload hdf5lib_destroy_all_filters(). Registering filters per-/O operation severely degrade performance. See Getting Started guide boilerplate code. Reader Must Plugin: compress dataset using external plugin (like Zstd LZ4), application opens file must also corresponding HDF5 plugin installed. generating files external users guarantee plugins installed, use built-gzip filter maximum portability.

title: Compression & Filters
text: applying filter via H5Pset_filter(plist_id, filter_id, flags, cd_nelmts, cd_values), must pass array unsigned int values known cd_values (Client Data Values). values configure specific behavior compressor. explicit configurations examples every filter bundled hdf5lib.

title: Compression & Filters
text: Recommendation: Use Maximum Portability. GZIP built directly core HDF5 library, meaning files compressed can read standard HDF5 installation globally without needing external plugins. However, significantly slower modern alternatives. Filter ID: H5Z_FILTER_DEFLATE (1) Elements (cd_nelmts): 1 cd_values[0]: Compression level 0 (none) 9 (maximum). need manually pack cd_values array GZIP. HDF5 provides dedicated helper function.
code: // Apply GZIP compression with level 9 H5Pset_deflate(plist_id, 9);

title: Compression & Filters
text: Recommendation: Use Default General-Purpose Compressor. Developed Facebook, Zstd provides compression ratios comparable better GZIP, substantially faster compression decompression speeds. Filter ID: 32015 Elements (cd_nelmts): 1 cd_values[0]: Compression level, 1 (fastest) 22 (best). Use 3 5 default; provide optimal balance speed file size, whereas levels 10 offer steeply diminishing returns significantly longer compression times.
code: unsigned int cd_values[1] = { 5 }; // Zstd level 5 H5Pset_filter(plist_id, 32015, H5Z_FLAG_MANDATORY, 1, cd_values);

title: Compression & Filters
text: Recommendation: Use Maximum Speed. LZ4 prioritizes extreme compression decompression speeds (often bottlenecked RAM bandwidth) finding absolute smallest file size. Ideal hot data, fast pipelines, real-time /O. Filter ID: 32004 Elements (cd_nelmts): 2 cd_values[0]: Reserved/padding (Pass 0). cd_values[1]: Compression level. Passing 0 uses standard, lightning-fast LZ4. Passing value >0 (e.g., 9) enables LZ4-HC (High Compression) mode.
code: unsigned int cd_values[2] = { 0, 9 }; // LZ4 High Compression H5Pset_filter(plist_id, 32004, H5Z_FLAG_MANDATORY, 2, cd_values);

title: Compression & Filters
text: Recommendation: Use Parallel Compression Complex Pipelines. Blosc2 utilizes internal thread pools compress blocks data parallel. also features Programmable Filter Pipeline, allowing chain 6 distinct pre-filters (e.g., Delta followed Bitshuffle) data hits final compressor. plugin implementation ensures even complex multi-filter pipelines remain 100% decodable standard h5py community plugins. Restrictions: using ZFP compressor codec (33, 34, 35), must pass floating-point data (float32 float64). Furthermore, filter applied data reaches ZFP completely corrupt dataset. must apply upstream filters natively HDF5 (e.g., H5Pset_shuffle), chain pre-filters internally within Blosc2 pipeline, ZFP target codec.

title: Compression & Filters
text: need one pre-filter, use standard 8-element configuration: Filter ID: 32026 Elements (cd_nelmts): 8 cd_values[0-3]: Reserved (Pass 0). cd_values[4]: Compression level (0 9). Note: Blosc2 enforces universal 0-9 scale. select codec wider range like Zstd, Blosc2 internally maps 0-9 value Zstd’s 1-22 scale. cd_values[5]: Pre-filter (0=nofilter, 1=shuffle, 2=bitshuffle, 3=delta, 4=truncprec). cd_values[6]: Compressor ID (0=blosclz, 1=lz4, 2=lz4hc, 3=snappy, 4=zlib, 5=zstd, 11=ndlz, 33=zfp_acc, 34=zfp_prec, 35=zfp_rate). using truncprec pre-filter (cd_values[5]=4), defines number bits precision keep (e.g., 16). using ZFP compressor (cd_values[6] 33, 34, 35), integer sets specific lossy parameter based chosen mode. See ZFP section guide choose mode set value.
code: // Blosc2 using ZFP Fixed Precision mode, keeping exactly 16 bits of precision unsigned int cd_values[8] = { 0, 0, 0, 0, 5, 0, 34, 16 };  H5Pset_filter(plist_id, 32026, H5Z_FLAG_MANDATORY, 8, cd_values);

title: Compression & Filters
text: chain multiple pre-filters, expand cd_values array. plugin automatically parse array dynamically translate dataset creation preserve strict layout compatibility. Elements (cd_nelmts): 8 + (2 * N), N number filters. cd_values[0-3]: Reserved (Pass 0). cd_values[4]: Compression level (0 9). cd_values[5]: Legacy fallback pre-filter (Typically matches last filter, e.g., 2 bitshuffle. Required legacy fallback). cd_values[6]: Compressor ID. cd_values[7]: Number pipeline filters N (maximum 6). cd_values[8 ... 8+N-1]: sequence Filter IDs (e.g., 3 Delta, 2 Bitshuffle). cd_values[8+N ... 8+2N-1]: Metadata respective filter (usually 0).
code: // Blosc2 Pipeline: Delta -> Bitshuffle -> Zstd (level 5) unsigned int cd_pipeline[12] = {0}; cd_pipeline[4] = 1; // Compression level (~3 on Zstd range) cd_pipeline[5] = 2; // Legacy fallback (Bitshuffle) cd_pipeline[6] = 5; // Compressor (Zstd)  cd_pipeline[7] = 2; // Number of pipeline filters  // Filter IDs cd_pipeline[8] = 3; // Filter 1: Delta cd_pipeline[9] = 2; // Filter 2: Bitshuffle  // Filter Metadata cd_pipeline[10] = 0; // Meta for Delta cd_pipeline[11] = 0; // Meta for Bitshuffle  H5Pset_filter(plist_id, 32026, H5Z_FLAG_MANDATORY, 12, cd_pipeline);

title: Compression & Filters
text: Recommendation: Use High-Speed Lossy Compression. ZFP mathematically simplifies multidimensional arrays achieve massive compression ratios. Use perfect bit--bit reconstruction required. Restrictions: ZFP strictly requires numeric, multidimensional arrays (natively supporting 32/64-bit integers 32/64-bit floats). filter applied data reaches ZFP completely corrupt dataset. must apply upstream HDF5 pre-filters (e.g., Shuffle, Bitshuffle, Scale-Offset) ZFP property list. (Note: ZFP can invoked codec within Blosc2 meta-compressor, restricts floating-point data limits available compression modes Accuracy, Precision, Rate. integer arrays, Expert mode, Reversible (lossless) mode, must use standalone ZFP plugin).

title: Compression & Filters
text: Fixed Accuracy: Defines strict absolute error tolerance. Passing 3 ensures decompressed value deviates original 10−310^{-3} (0.001), regardless whether number huge tiny. Fixed Precision: Defines sliding scale detail. Passing 16 keeps roughly 5 digits detail scaled proportionally size number, allowing larger absolute errors massive numbers tiny absolute errors microscopic fractions. Fixed Rate: Defines strict storage limit. Passing 8 forces compressor use exactly 8 bits storage per value, guaranteeing highly predictable file size. Expert: Allows manual configuration underlying ZFP parameters (minbits, maxbits, maxprec, minexp) advanced users requiring highly specific encoding profiles. Reversible: Provides perfectly lossless compression, guaranteeing exact bit--bit reconstruction original numerical array.

title: Compression & Filters
text: Filter ID: 32013 Elements (cd_nelmts): 6 cd_values[0]: compression mode (1=Rate, 2=Precision, 3=Accuracy, 4=Expert, 5=Reversible/Lossless). cd_values[1-5]: Mode-specific parameters. instance, Precision mode (cd_values[0]=2), cd_values[2] specifies bits precision keep, padding rest zeros (e.g., {2, 0, 16, 0, 0, 0}). can manually pack 6-element cd_values array, ZFP plugin exposes convenient external helper functions can declare C code set parameters effortlessly.
code: // Declare the external helpers provided by the bundled ZFP plugin extern herr_t H5Pset_zfp_rate(hid_t plist, double rate); extern herr_t H5Pset_zfp_precision(hid_t plist, unsigned int prec); extern herr_t H5Pset_zfp_accuracy(hid_t plist, double acc); extern herr_t H5Pset_zfp_expert(hid_t plist, unsigned int minbits, unsigned int maxbits, unsigned int maxprec, int minexp); extern herr_t H5Pset_zfp_reversible(hid_t plist); // Lossless mode  // ... later in your code ...  // Compress data using ZFP's Accuracy mode (maintaining 0.001 tolerance) H5Pset_zfp_accuracy(plist_id, 0.001);

title: Compression & Filters
text: Recommendation: Use Boost Compression Structured Data. Bitshuffle standalone compressor; pre-filter transposes bits structured arrays (like integers, floats, compound datatypes) expose redundancy, handing data internal compressor (LZ4 Zstd). vastly improves compression ratios highly structured datasets. Filter ID: 32008 Elements (cd_nelmts): 3 cd_values[0]: Block size. Pass 0 let library choose optimal default (usually 1024). cd_values[1]: Compressor algorithm. 0 = raw bitshuffling (compression), 2 = LZ4, 3 = Zstd. cd_values[2]: Compression level. applies Zstd selected (e.g., 5). Pass 0 uncompressed LZ4.
code: // Bitshuffle data, then apply Zstd compression at level 5 unsigned int cd_values[3] = { 0, 3, 5 };  H5Pset_filter(plist_id, 32008, H5Z_FLAG_MANDATORY, 3, cd_values);

title: Compression & Filters
text: Recommendation: Use Backwards Compatibility. Blosc v1 pioneering meta-compressor, entirely superseded Blosc2 (faster, smarter, supports features). filter bundled strictly ensure backward compatibility reading older HDF5 files. Use Blosc2 new development. Filter ID: 32001 Elements (cd_nelmts): 7 cd_values[0-3]: Reserved (Pass 0). cd_values[4]: Compression level (0 9). Note: Blosc enforces universal 0-9 scale. select codec wider range like Zstd, Blosc internally maps 0-9 value Zstd’s 1-22 scale. cd_values[5]: Pre-filter (0=nofilter, 1=byte shuffle, 2=bit shuffle). cd_values[6]: Compressor ID (0=blosclz, 1=lz4, 2=lz4hc, 3=snappy, 4=zlib, 5=zstd).
code: // Blosc v1 using LZ4 (level 5) and the standard byte shuffle pre-filter unsigned int cd_values[7] = { 0, 0, 0, 0, 5, 1, 1 };  H5Pset_filter(plist_id, 32001, H5Z_FLAG_MANDATORY, 7, cd_values);

title: Compression & Filters
text: Recommendation: Use Backwards Compatibility. Historically used legacy NASA Earthdata datasets, original SZIP algorithm carried strict licensing encumbrances stifled widespread adoption. Modern tools like ZFP Blosc2 vastly superior scientific data. included primarily reading legacy archives (note: hdf5lib safely circumvents historical licensing issues bundling libaec, permissively licensed, drop-replacement). Restrictions: SZIP strictly requires numeric data (integers floating-point numbers). support compound datatypes, strings, variable-length arrays. chunk size (elements) must also exact multiple block size. Filter ID: H5Z_FILTER_SZIP (4) Elements (cd_nelmts): 2 cd_values[0]: Options mask (e.g., H5_SZIP_NN_OPTION_MASK H5_SZIP_EC_OPTION_MASK). cd_values[1]: Pixels per block. Must even, typically 8, 16, 32. Like GZIP, SZIP dedicated helper function.
code: // Apply SZIP compression (Entropy Coding method, 8 pixels per block) H5Pset_szip(plist_id, H5_SZIP_EC_OPTION_MASK, 8);

title: Compression & Filters
text: Recommendation: Use Backwards Compatibility. BZIP2 historically offered fantastic compression ratios, notoriously slow compress decompress. Zstd now achieves comparable better ratios fraction time. Bundled strictly allow reading legacy archives. Filter ID: 307 Elements (cd_nelmts): 1 cd_values[0]: Block size / Compression level 1 (fastest) 9 (best). Default 9.
code: unsigned int cd_values[1] = { 9 }; // BZIP2 level 9 H5Pset_filter(plist_id, 307, H5Z_FLAG_MANDATORY, 1, cd_values);

title: Compression & Filters
text: Recommendation: Use Backwards Compatibility. LZF Snappy early pioneers extreme-speed compression. However, LZ4 generally outperforms modern environments. LZF included primarily default high-speed compressor early versions Python h5py library. LZF Snappy extremely fast, low-overhead algorithms. require zero configuration parameters. LZF Filter ID: 32000 Snappy Filter ID: 32003 Elements (cd_nelmts): 0
code: // Apply Snappy compression H5Pset_filter(plist_id, 32003, H5Z_FLAG_MANDATORY, 0, NULL);

title: Integration Guide
text: many R package developers, writing native C code using R’s .Call interface preferred way interact C libraries, avoids compilation overhead abstraction layers C++. use hdf5lib natively, ensure LinkingTo: hdf5lib DESCRIPTION file, src/Makevars set compiler linker flags. following example demonstrates native C function designed called R. creates HDF5 file, sets dataset Zstandard (Zstd) compression filter, writes data .
code: #include <R.h> #include <Rinternals.h> #include <hdf5.h>  // Remember to call hdf5lib_register_all_filters() in your R package's .onLoad!  SEXP write_zstd_native(SEXP r_filename, SEXP r_dsetname) {     const char *filename = CHAR(STRING_ELT(r_filename, 0));     const char *dsetname = CHAR(STRING_ELT(r_dsetname, 0));          int data[1000];     for(int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) data[i] = i;     hsize_t dims[1] = { 1000 };      hid_t file_id = H5Fcreate(filename, H5F_ACC_TRUNC, H5P_DEFAULT, H5P_DEFAULT);     hid_t space_id = H5Screate_simple(1, dims, NULL);     hid_t dcpl_id = H5Pcreate(H5P_DATASET_CREATE);      // 1. Enable chunking (Required for all filters)     hsize_t chunk_dims[1] = { 100 };     H5Pset_chunk(dcpl_id, 1, chunk_dims);      // 2. Apply Zstandard Filter (Filter ID: 32015)     // cd_values[0] = Compression Level (e.g., 5)     unsigned int cd_values[1] = { 5 };      H5Pset_filter(dcpl_id, 32015, H5Z_FLAG_MANDATORY, 1, cd_values);      hid_t dset_id = H5Dcreate2(file_id, dsetname, H5T_NATIVE_INT,                                 space_id, H5P_DEFAULT, dcpl_id, H5P_DEFAULT);      H5Dwrite(dset_id, H5T_NATIVE_INT, H5S_ALL, H5S_ALL, H5P_DEFAULT, data);      H5Pclose(dcpl_id);     H5Dclose(dset_id);     H5Sclose(space_id);     H5Fclose(file_id);          return R_NilValue; }

code: if (!require("hdf5lib")) install.packages("hdf5lib")  c_file <- "get_version.c" so_file <- paste0("get_version", .Platform$dynlib.ext)  # Set environment variables for the compiler Sys.setenv(     PKG_CPPFLAGS = hdf5lib::c_flags(),     PKG_LIBS = hdf5lib::ld_flags() )  # Construct and run the compilation command R_EXE <- file.path(R.home("bin"), "R") compile_cmd <- sprintf('%s CMD SHLIB %s', shQuote(R_EXE), shQuote(c_file))  system(compile_cmd)  # Clean up environment variables Sys.unsetenv(c("PKG_CPPFLAGS", "PKG_LIBS"))  # Load the shared library and call the C function dyn.load(so_file) version <- .Call("get_version_c")  print(version) dyn.unload(so_file)

title: Parallel Programming
text: following C code defines worker function opens existing HDF5 file writes unique dataset. spawn multiple pthreads main .Call entry point execute workers concurrently.
code: #include <R.h> #include <Rinternals.h> #include <pthread.h> #include <hdf5.h> #include <stdio.h> #include <stdlib.h>  // Structure to pass data to our threads typedef struct {     const char* filename;     int thread_id; } ThreadData;  // The thread worker function void* worker_func(void* arg) {     ThreadData* data = (ThreadData*)arg;          char dset_name[64];     snprintf(dset_name, sizeof(dset_name), "thread_%d", data->thread_id);     int value = data->thread_id;     hsize_t dims[1] = {1};      // HDF5's thread-safety guarantees these low-level calls are safe     hid_t file_id = H5Fopen(data->filename, H5F_ACC_RDWR, H5P_DEFAULT);     if (file_id >= 0) {         hid_t space_id = H5Screate_simple(1, dims, NULL);         hid_t dset_id = H5Dcreate2(file_id, dset_name, H5T_NATIVE_INT,                                    space_id, H5P_DEFAULT, H5P_DEFAULT, H5P_DEFAULT);                  if (dset_id >= 0) {             H5Dwrite(dset_id, H5T_NATIVE_INT, H5S_ALL, H5S_ALL, H5P_DEFAULT, &value);             H5Dclose(dset_id);         }         H5Sclose(space_id);         H5Fclose(file_id);     }     return NULL; }  // Main entry point for R's .Call interface SEXP parallel_write_native(SEXP r_filename, SEXP r_nthreads) {     const char* filename = CHAR(STRING_ELT(r_filename, 0));     int n_threads = asInteger(r_nthreads);          // Create the file sequentially before spawning threads     hid_t file_id = H5Fcreate(filename, H5F_ACC_TRUNC, H5P_DEFAULT, H5P_DEFAULT);     if (file_id < 0) Rf_error("Failed to create HDF5 file.");     H5Fclose(file_id);      // Allocate memory for threads and data     pthread_t* threads = (pthread_t*)malloc(n_threads * sizeof(pthread_t));     ThreadData* tdata = (ThreadData*)malloc(n_threads * sizeof(ThreadData));      // Spawn threads     for (int i = 0; i < n_threads; i++) {         tdata[i].filename = filename;         tdata[i].thread_id = i;         pthread_create(&threads[i], NULL, worker_func, &tdata[i]);     }      // Wait for all threads to complete     for (int i = 0; i < n_threads; i++) {         pthread_join(threads[i], NULL);     }      free(threads);     free(tdata);      return R_NilValue; }

title: Parallel Programming
text: following C++ code defines “worker” struct writes simple dataset using thread-safe low-level API. RcppParallel::parallelFor executes worker multiple threads, thread writing different dataset. hdf5lib enables thread-safety, internal mutexes within HDF5 library serialize low-level API calls, preventing race condition.
code: #include <Rcpp.h> #include <RcppParallel.h> #include <hdf5.h>  struct H5Writer : public RcppParallel::Worker {     const std::string filename;      H5Writer(const std::string filename) : filename(filename) {}      void operator()(std::size_t begin, std::size_t end) {         for (std::size_t i = begin; i < end; i++) {             // Each thread works on a different dataset             std::string dset_name = "thread_" + std::to_string(i);             int data = static_cast<int>(i);             hsize_t dims = {1};              // HDF5's thread-safety guarantees these LL calls are safe             hid_t file_id = H5Fopen(filename.c_str(), H5F_ACC_RDWR, H5P_DEFAULT);             if (file_id < 0) continue;              hid_t space_id = H5Screate_simple(1, dims, NULL);             hid_t dset_id = H5Dcreate2(file_id, dset_name.c_str(), H5T_NATIVE_INT,                                      space_id, H5P_DEFAULT, H5P_DEFAULT, H5P_DEFAULT);              if (dset_id >= 0) {                 H5Dwrite(dset_id, H5T_NATIVE_INT, H5S_ALL, H5S_ALL, H5P_DEFAULT, &data);                 H5Dclose(dset_id);             }              H5Sclose(space_id);             H5Fclose(file_id);         }     } };  //' Write to an HDF5 file in parallel //' @param filename Path to the HDF5 file. //' @param n_threads Number of threads to use. //' @export // [[Rcpp::export]] void parallel_write(std::string filename, int n_threads) {     // Create the file first     hid_t file_id = H5Fcreate(filename.c_str(), H5F_ACC_TRUNC, H5P_DEFAULT, H5P_DEFAULT);     if (file_id < 0) Rcpp::stop("Failed to create file.");     H5Fclose(file_id);      H5Writer writer(filename);     RcppParallel::parallelFor(0, n_threads, writer); }

title: Headers and Static Libraries for HDF5
text: hdf5lib R package provides self-contained, static build HDF5 C library (release 2.0.0). sole purpose allow R packages easily link HDF5 without requiring users install system-level dependencies, thereby ensuring consistent reliable build process across major platforms. package provides R functions intended R package developers use LinkingTo field DESCRIPTION file.

title: Headers and Static Libraries for HDF5
text: Zero-Dependency & CRAN-Ready: Builds HDF5 library source using standard R build tools. guarantees package works “box” operating system without requiring users install system-level libraries hold administrative privileges. Comprehensive Core API (v2.1.0): Provides complete access HDF5 C API, including Low-Level simplified High-Level interfaces, giving full control file structure, metadata, raw /O. State---Art Compression Built-: Bundles extensive suite compression filters directly within package. Alongside native gzip/deflate szip, package gains immediate access high-performance plugins like Zstandard (Zstd), LZ4, Blosc/Blosc2, Snappy, ZFP, Bzip2, LZF, Bitshuffle - without relying external system libraries. API Version Locking: Protect package future breaking changes. Downstream packages can selectively compile specific HDF5 API versions (e.g., 2.0, 1.14, 1.12), ensuring long-term stability predictable build cycle. Safe Parallel Processing: Compiled thread-safety enabled default. prevents data corruption integrating multi-threaded R frameworks like RcppParallel. (Note: External file locking still required use High-Level APIs, thread-safe, access files across multiple independent processes).

title: Headers and Static Libraries for HDF5
text: utilize bundled compression plugins (LZ4, Zstd, Blosc, etc.), must registered HDF5 library. registering filters modifies global state spins background thread pools (via Blosc2), never register filters per-/O basis, severely impact performance. Instead, expose registration functions R call exactly package’s load/unload cycle. Create C Wrappers (e.g., src/init.c): Hook R Package Load (e.g., R/zzz.R):
code: #include <Rinternals.h> #include "hdf5lib.h"  SEXP r_register_hdf5_filters() {     hdf5lib_register_all_filters();     return R_NilValue; }  SEXP r_destroy_hdf5_filters() {     hdf5lib_destroy_all_filters();     return R_NilValue; } .onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {     # Register plugins and spin up Blosc thread pools once per session     .Call("r_register_hdf5_filters", PACKAGE = pkgname) }  .onUnload <- function(libpath) {     # Cleanly tear down threads and free memory to prevent Valgrind warnings     .Call("r_destroy_hdf5_filters", PACKAGE = "myrpackage") }

Note: maintain zero-dependency footprint, optional features requiring external system libraries - Parallel HDF5 (MPI), HDFS, S3 support - included. full core API available, following highlights represent commonly used modules:

title: Headers and Static Libraries for HDF5
text: HL APIs provide “lite” versions complex operations, making significantly easier perform common tasks without manual memory hyperslab management. H5LT (Lite): Simplified dataset attribute operations (e.g., H5LTmake_dataset_int, H5LTread_dataset_double, H5LTget_dataset_info). H5IM (Image): Standardized functions working image data (e.g., H5IMmake_image_24bit, H5IMread_image). H5TB (Table): Functions creating manipulating tabular data structures (e.g., H5TBmake_table, H5TBappend_records).

title: Headers and Static Libraries for HDF5
text: package exposes full range core HDF5 modules fine-grained control file structure, metadata, raw /O: H5F (File): Manage file lifecycle (H5Fcreate, H5Fopen, H5Fclose, etc.). H5G (Group): Organize objects within file (H5Gcreate2, H5Gopen2, H5Gclose, etc.). H5D (Dataset): Manage raw data arrays /O (H5Dcreate2, H5Dread, H5Dwrite, etc.). H5S (Dataspace): Define data dimensions selections (H5Screate_simple, H5Sselect_hyperslab, etc.). H5T (Datatype): Define manage data types (e.g., H5T_NATIVE_INT, H5Tcopy, H5Tinsert). H5A (Attribute): Manage metadata attached objects (H5Acreate2, H5Aread, H5Awrite). H5P (Property List): Configure library behavior, chunking compression (H5Pcreate, H5Pset_chunk). Note: complete list available functions, please refer official HDF5 Reference Manual. function documented can called package including headers shown .

title: Headers and Static Libraries for HDF5
text: Rhdf5lib package also provides HDF5 C library. hdf5lib created provide general-purpose, standalone HDF5 library provider offers several key distinctions: Zero Configuration Installation: hdf5lib designed simplicity. Installation via install.packages() requires user configuration reliably provides modern HDF5 build important features enabled default. Rhdf5lib, flexible, requires users manage compile-time configuration options customized build. Modern HDF5 Version: hdf5lib bundles HDF5 v2.1.0, providing access latest features fixes, including native complex number support improved UTF-8 handling Windows. recent version typically bundled Rhdf5lib (v1.12.2 Bioconductor 3.19). Thread-Safety Enabled: hdf5lib builds HDF5 thread-safety enabled, ensuring safe use parallel R packages (like RcppParallel). Rhdf5lib support building feature. Predictable Versioning Features: version hdf5lib directly corresponds bundled HDF5 version (e.g., hdf5lib v2.1.0.x bundles HDF5 v2.1.0). allows developers require minimum hdf5lib version guarantee specific HDF5 version consistent set features. contrast, Rhdf5lib may link pre-existing system library configured install-time, package version guarantee version HDF5 actually use features enabled. hdf5lib intended simple reliable provider HDF5 C library R package.
